transcript: I was not familiar with comedian Gary Gulman before I attended his new show with the Lucille Lortel last night. I don't think I'm the most qualified to critique stand up comedy, but Grandiloquent is certainly a well-rehearsed show and presents an overarching story. It’s primarily an explanation and exploration of Gary's self-described grandiloquence, as told through some core memories from childhood and the ways those experiences shaped his relationship to comedy and validation. Gary has a very likable presence and there's something charming about the way he uses the most unnecessarily robust vocabulary to recount the thoughts and feelings he was having in first grade. This is the focus of much the show, and I found the whole vibe to be very nostalgic. The focus frays a bit in the last third of the show, and the end wasn't quite as satisfying as I hoped, but overall it was still enjoyable — I laughed and I felt, which I think is the point. With that, another program for my collection.
